lit.\u0027¿Qué orienta el –NO₂ en una SEAr?\: "What does –NO₂ direct to in an SEAr?"
lit.\u0027\u003c/table\u003e\u003cp class=\":
"

The energies are schematic (carbocations in solution); they serve to reason about the trend, not for quantitative predictions.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eMarkovnikov\u003c/b\u: "Markovnikov: the H goes to the C with more H atoms; most stable carbocation (3° > 2° > 1°)."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003e\u003cb\u003eMarkovni:
"

Markovnikov: in the addition of HX to an unsymmetrical alkene, the H bonds to the carbon that already has more hydrogens. Modern explanation: the path through the more stable carbocation (lower transition-state energy) is much faster. Comparison: secondary (left) versus primary (right).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon \u003cb\u003eBr₂\:
"

With Br₂ no free carbocation forms but a cyclic bromonium ion (Br⁺ bridge over C–C). Br⁻ attacks from the opposite face (SN2 on the bromonium): the addition is anti, stereospecific. Product: 1,2-dibromopropane.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl anillo es poco nuc:
"

The ring is only weakly nucleophilic: it requires a powerful electrophile, generated with Lewis or Brønsted acids (HNO₃/H₂SO₄ → NO₂⁺). The π electrons attack the electrophile and momentarily destroy the aromaticity: this is the slow step.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl benceno tiene 6 e⁻:
"

Benzene has 6 delocalized π electrons (blue ring): great stability (≈ 150 kJ/mol of resonance energy). An addition would destroy the aromaticity; that is why it reacts by electrophilic aromatic substitution (SEAr): the H is replaced by an electrophile and the ring is recovered. Example: nitration with NO₂⁺.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl doble enlace C=C t:
"

The C=C double bond has π electron density exposed above and below the plane (blue cloud). It is an electron-rich region: a nucleophile. Typical reactions are electrophilic additions: the π bond breaks and two new σ bonds form. Here: propene + HBr.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl intermedio es el \:
"

The intermediate is the σ complex (arenium ion): the attacked carbon is sp³ (with H and E) and the + charge is delocalized over the carbons ortho and para to it (red spheres). It is the analog of the carbocation in the addition, but with resonance stabilization (3 structures).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl intermedio es un \:
"

The intermediate is a carbocation: a planar sp² carbon with an empty p orbital (orange lobes) perpendicular to the plane. Here it is secondary: stabilized by hyperconjugation (neighboring σ C–H bonds donating into the empty p) and by the inductive effect of the alkyl groups. Tertiary > secondary > primary.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl nucleófilo \u003cb:
"

The Br⁻ nucleophile donates an electron pair to the empty p orbital and forms the C–Br bond. It can attack from either face of the planar carbocation; if the product were chiral a racemic mixture would be obtained. Product: 2-bromopropane.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eGrupos \u003cb\u003ed:
"

Donor groups (–CH₃, –OH) enrich the ring (red cloud), stabilize the σ complex and speed up SEAr (toluene ≈ 25× benzene). Withdrawing groups (–NO₂) deplete the ring (blue cloud) and slow it (nitrobenzene ≈ 6×10⁻⁸ × benzene). –Cl deactivates (inductive) but directs o/p (resonance).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos electrones π atac:
"

The π electrons attack the δ⁺ hydrogen of HBr (curved arrow); the H–Br bond breaks and Br takes the electron pair as Br⁻. The H bonds to the less substituted carbon, leaving the positive charge on the more substituted one. This is the rate-determining step.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn sustituyente ya pr:
"

A substituent already present directs the new electrophile. The bars show the typical distribution for nitration: –CH₃ directs ortho/para (58 % o, 5 % m, 37 % p); –NO₂ directs meta (93 %). Reason: the stability of the σ complex (can the substituent stabilize the + charge?).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUna base (HSO₄⁻) arra:
"

A base (HSO₄⁻) removes the H⁺ from the sp³ carbon; the electrons of the C–H bond return to the ring and aromaticity is recovered. The net result is substitution: Ar–H + E⁺ → Ar–E + H⁺. The step is fast because recovering the aromatic ring is very favorable.

"
